matrix-hookshot is a Matrix bot for connecting to external services like GitHub, GitLab, JIRA, and more. Prior to 7.3.3, Hookshot can crash in src/Bridge.ts while processing a modern Matrix reply whose m.relates_to.m.in_reply_to.event_id identifies an event that the bot cannot read. Bridge event handling calls botClient.getEvent() for the parent event without catching the resulting M_NOT_FOUND error, allowing the rejected request to escape reply processing and terminate the service. This issue is fixed in version 7.3.3.

Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3, contain a Missing Authorization vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Unauthorized access.

Bludit is vulnerable to Path Traversal in the page deletion functionality. An authenticated user with the Author role can set the UUID field of their own page to contain path traversal sequences (.. and path separators), which are saved without proper validation. When the page is deleted, Pages::delete() passes the path constructed from this UUID to Filesystem::deleteRecursive() without verifying that it still points to an allowed directory, allowing the attacker to delete any files, even not belonging to them. Critically, it is possible to delete admin pages and render the site unusable.


Because vendor contact attempts were unsuccessful, the vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.22.0 but may also affect other versions.

In the Aliro access control reference
  applications of the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door Lock and Access Control
  Add-on v1.0.0 through v1.1.1, the stored Access Document record does not
  retain validFrom and validUntil. The cached public key path (VerifyPublicKey())
  and the Kpersistent fast path (_VerifyKPersistentKey()) therefore never
  re-evaluate the Access Document validity period. An attacker who held a
  time-limited Aliro credential that was valid when first presented can
  continue to obtain physical access after the Access Document has expired, for
  as long as the cached record remains available. Fixed in v1.2.0.

In
the Matter and Aliro Door Lock Application of the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door
Lock and Access Control Add-on v1.0.0 through v1.1.1 with
CONFIG_DOOR_LOCK_STEP_UP_PHASE enabled, deleting a Credential Issuer passes the
1-based Matter credential index to ClearValidityIterations(), which expects a
0-based storage index. The intended issuer's ValidityIteration state is left in
place, and the state of the adjacent, still-provisioned issuer is cleared. This
resets that issuer's rollback protection. An attacker holding an older but correctly
signed Access Document from the adjacent issuer, whose validity iteration had
been superseded, can then potentially obtain physical access. Fixed in v1.2.0.

In the Matter door lock applications of
  the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door Lock and Access Control Add-on v1.0.0
  through v1.1.1, AccessManager::ValidateCredential() checks only credential
  occupancy and the secret bytes, and never reads the owning user's UserStatus.
  It also returns success when no owning user can be resolved. A user suspended
  by setting their status to OccupiedDisabled can continue to unlock the door
  with their previously assigned credential, and an orphaned but occupied
  credential is also accepted. Fixed in v1.2.0.

fzf is a command-line fuzzy finder. Prior to 0.74.5, bin/fzf-tmux validates separately supplied layout sizes but does not validate attached -l and -u layout values before Bash arithmetic expansion, allowing command substitution in a crafted operand to execute as the invoking user during option parsing. The same validation failure lets space-bearing popup geometry options -x, -y, -w, -h, and -p reach an unquoted tmux popup option string and inject additional tmux flags. Exploitation requires less-trusted project configuration, a wrapper, or a plugin to supply the poisoned value and requires the victim to invoke fzf-tmux; normal values are usually trusted, and the script has been superseded by built-in tmux options. This issue is fixed in version 0.74.5.

llama.cpp MTMD Multimodal GGUF File Parsing Integer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of llama.cpp. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of audio multimodal projector GGUF files. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in an integer overflow before allocating a buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-30980.

Storyden before 1.26.17 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the AccountRemoveRole handler that allows non-administrator users with MANAGE_ROLES to remove administrator roles. Attackers can send DELETE requests to the account roles endpoint to demote other administrators, potentially leaving the instance with no administrator.

Pleasanter contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in Publishing feature. If this vulnerability is exploited, a remote unauthenticated attacker who can access a site published using the product may obtain, by sending a specially crafted request, information on records of unpublished sites (e.g., titles), as well as the names of users, groups, and organizations registered in the same tenant. Note that the vulnerability only affects configurations where both of the following conditions are met: a site is published using the Publishing feature, and the published site contains link items (items linked to other sites, users, groups, or organizations).

Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Plug.Parsers.MULTIPART in elixir-plug plug allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust memory via a multipart request body built from parts without headers, or from header lines without a name and a value. The parser charges the :length limit only with the name and value bytes of each part header and the bytes of each part body. The part delimiter, the header separator, and the line endings cost nothing.

In lib/plug/parsers/multipart.ex, Plug.Parsers.MULTIPART.parse_multipart_headers/5 keeps an entry for every part without a content-disposition header, together with its header list, until the whole body is read. A request made of such parts does not reach the limit at any size, and the parser process holds a multiple of the request size in memory until parsing completes. Any endpoint that uses Plug.Parsers with the :multipart parser is reachable.

This issue affects plug: from 1.13.0 before 1.20.4.

This vulnerability exists in e-Sushrut HMIS due to the exposure of internal hospital operational statistics through data structure embedded in the HTML response of the login page. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by accessing the affected login page and extracting the returned HTML content.

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to gain unauthorized access to internal hospital operational information associated with the targeted healthcare organization.

Kadence Security plugin for WordPress (better-wp-security) before 10.0.6.1 contains a brute-force protection bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to evade per-host login lockouts by exploiting IPv6 address handling in ITSEC_Lib::get_ip(), which keys failed-login counters on the full 128-bit IPv6 address rather than a /64 prefix. Attackers who control a routed IPv6 /64 can send each login attempt from a new address within that prefix, resetting the per-host counter each time to perform password spraying and username enumeration, and can similarly evade the auto_ban_admin immediate ban via address rotation.

WPS Limit Login (wps-limit-login) before 1.5.9.5 contains an improper access control vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass login lockout protections by keying the per-attempt login counter and lockout map on the raw, non-canonicalized IPv6 client address. Attackers controlling a routable IPv6 /64 prefix can send each login attempt from a fresh address within that range, preventing any counter from reaching the lockout threshold and enabling effectively unlimited brute-force password guessing against WordPress accounts.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not authenticate callers of the ServerMMS2 AssetDiscoSimplifiedInfoSubmit operation. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can overwrite the asset data recorded for any appliance.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not authenticate callers of the MaintActionGet operation. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can read and cancel the pending maintenance actions of any appliance.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not authenticate callers of the ServerII2 remoteControlMSPAStartEndTimeSubmit operation. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can alter the recorded state and times of Take Control remote control tasks and the associated audit log entries.

The password reset function in N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 returns distinguishable responses for valid and invalid accounts. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can enumerate the email addresses of valid user accounts.

Contiki-NG through 5.2 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in coap_remove_observer_by_uri() that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to read past the supplied URI buffer. Attackers can send a CoAP GET Observe request with a Uri-Path shorter than an existing observer's URL, causing memcmp with strlen to read beyond the non-NUL-terminated buffer.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains an integer underflow in gf_xml_sax_parse_intern() in src/utils/xml_parser.c that causes a heap-based buffer overflow when completing partially buffered entities. Attackers can convince a user to process a crafted XML or XMT file with MP4Box, overflowing xml_sax_append_string() size arithmetic to corrupt heap memory and crash the process.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in gf_filter_pid_resolve_file_template_ex() in src/filter_core/filter_pid.c that allows local attackers to write past fixed GF_MAX_PATH stack buffers. Attackers can convince a user to segment a crafted NHML input referencing an overly long media file name with MP4Box -dash to crash the process.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in the XMT scene loader that allows local attackers to corrupt memory by supplying unbalanced command buffer closing elements. Attackers can convince a user to open a crafted XMT-A file with MP4Box, causing xmt_node_end() to treat a GF_Command as an SFCommandBuffer and crash the process.

GPAC through 26.07.0 contains a use of uninitialized variable vulnerability in xmt_parse_element() that allows local attackers to corrupt memory by supplying duplicate PROTO field names. Attackers can trick a user into opening a crafted XMT file with MP4Box, causing xmt_parse_sf_field() to write through an uninitialized pointer and crash the process.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT scene loader that leaves dangling MFURL pointers when xmt_node_end() discards nodes. Attackers can convince a user to open a crafted XMT file with MP4Box, causing xmt_resolve_od_links() to access freed heap memory and crash the process.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_parse_element() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that frees a node when a DEF attribute names a previously referenced undefined node. Attackers can convince a user to process a crafted XMT file with MP4Box, causing freed heap memory to be used and crashing the process.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in load_xmt_done() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that releases references for duplicate node stack entries. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT-A scene file encoded with MP4Box to crash the process and potentially corrupt heap memory.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_parse_element() that allows attackers to corrupt memory by supplying XMT-A elements that define and use the same node identifier. Attackers can craft an XMT scene file processed by MP4Box so xmt_text_content() accesses the freed node, crashing the process and possibly corrupting heap memory.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_parse_command() in loader_xmt.c that allows attackers to access freed memory via a dangling command buffer pointer. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene file whose Replace command frees a Conditional node, crashing MP4Box and potentially corrupting the heap.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains an invalid pointer free vulnerability in gf_sg_command_del() in src/scenegraph/commands.c that allows attackers to corrupt the heap via crafted XMT scene files. Attackers can supply an XMT-A file whose command field_ptr references the embedded new_node member, causing free() on an interior address and crashing MP4Box.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds read vulnerability in xmt_parse_mf_field() in loader_xmt.c caused by unchecked cursor advancement when splitting multi-value XMT-A fields. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene file opened with MP4Box to make xmt_parse_string() read past the heap buffer and crash the process.

wishthis through 1.2.3 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the PUT branch of src/api/wishes.php that allows unauthenticated attackers to modify wish URLs across all users. Attackers who know a wish link from a public wishlist can supply wish_url_current and wish_url_proposed parameters to redirect owners and gift-givers to attacker-controlled URLs.

Pika before 1.5.0 contains an uncontrolled resource allocation vulnerability that allows malicious brokers to exhaust client memory by declaring oversized frame payloads. Attackers can send frame headers declaring up to 4 GiB payloads, unchecked against frame_max, or very large message bodies to terminate consuming applications.

Gargoyle 2023.1 through 2026.1.1 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the bundled Plus interpreter's ReadAction() function in terps/plus/loaddatabase.c, which never bounds-checks the index into the 1024-entry conditions array. Attackers can supply a crafted or truncated .plus game file with unterminated action conditions to write file-controlled values past the array and crash the player.

In OpenStack Cinder before 29.1.1, by making an os-initialize_connection request with an IQN that includes a path traversal as part of the connector's initiator element, an authenticated user with a 'member' role may create or overwrite files in the volume host filesystem. Only cinder-volume hosts using the LIO iSCSI target driver are affected. This target driver is typically used with the LVM volume driver.

pretix provides a mechanism where ticket QR codes are cryptographically signed and can be verified by our pretixSCAN apps in offline mode without any database of valid tickets. pretixSCAN checks the signature to verify that the ticket was issued by the correct pretix event and compares the QR code against a list of revoked QR codes. A QR code becomes revoked when the order is canceled, or the ticket is changed in a way that a new QR code needs to be generated.




However, the parsing of the QR code in all of our pretixSCAN apps contained a faulty computation, rendering the check for the correct length of the contents faulty. This way, an attacker is able to craft multiple QR codes for the same ticket which have the same content, but look different and therefore do not match against the revocation list. This does not allow to fabricate entirely new tickets, but it does allow to enter the event with e.g. a canceled ticket. This attack requires pretixSCAN to be scanning in offline mode and the "pretix signature scheme 1" to be used for the event's QR codes.




If the attack is executed, the ticket unfortunately shows as valid (green) on the scanner but as invalid (red) on the server since the server later cannot match it to a ticket. We scanned the entire database of scans on pretix Hosted and could not find any traces of this being exploited in the past.

GPAC 26.02.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in dasher_configure_pid() in src/filters/dasher.c that dereferences ds2->set without checking for NULL. Attackers can supply a crafted MPEG-2 TS file processed with MP4Box -dash to disconnect a PID and crash MP4Box, causing denial of service.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains an uninitialized pointer access vulnerability in GetESD() in src/isomedia/track.c that allows attackers to trigger invalid memory reads via crafted MP4 files. Attackers can supply an MP4 with an rvcc box having predefined_rvc_config set to 0 and no meta item index, causing strcmp() on an uninitialized mime_type pointer and crashing MP4Box -add.

GPAC before 26.02.0 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in m2tsdmx_send_packet() in src/filters/dmx_m2ts.c caused by double-skipping the VC-1 start-code offset. Attackers can supply a crafted MPEG-2 TS VC-1 stream that underflows the remaining length, causing memcpy() to over-read and crash MP4Box on import.

GPAC before 26.02.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in gf_filter_pid_set_args_internal() that leaves a stale pointer after gf_props_reset_single() frees a parsed PID property value. Attackers can supply a crafted filelist input processed by MP4Box with -add, causing gf_props_del_property() to access freed memory and crash the application.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in gf_mpd_resolve_url() in src/media_tools/mpd.c that allows attackers to write past a heap buffer via crafted DASH manifests. Attackers can supply a crafted MPD whose segment template expands beyond the allocation through unchecked strcat() calls, crashing MP4Box and causing denial of service.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in dasher_gather_deps() in src/filters/dasher.c that fails to detect cyclic stream dependency chains. Attackers can supply a crafted MPEG-2 TS file that MP4Box processes with -dash, exhausting the stack and crashing the process for denial of service.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in xmt_new_od_link_from_node() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that allows attackers to crash the process. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene file with an MFURL object-descriptor link lacking an OD ID and name, crashing MP4Box for denial of service.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in xmt_parse_element() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that allows attackers to crash the process via ROUTE elements. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT-A scene file placing a ROUTE element before any scene command creates an access unit, crashing MP4Box during encoding and causing denial of service.

Phoboslab pl_mpeg through commit c871f2b contains an integer underflow in plm_demux_seek() that allows attackers to trigger heap out-of-bounds reads via crafted MPEG-PS files. Attackers can supply a PES packet with payload under 6 bytes, wrapping the packet->length - 6 loop bound during force_intra seeking to crash applications.

SOIL2 before 1.4.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in its DDS, PVR and PKM image loaders that write results through unchecked caller-supplied output pointers. Attackers can supply a valid DDS, PVR or PKM file to applications passing NULL output pointers to SOIL_load_image or stbi_info, causing a crash.

Gargoyle 2023.1 through 2026.1.1 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in the bundled Plus interpreter's ReadString() function in terps/plus/loaddatabase.c that fails to handle end of file. Attackers can supply an empty, truncated, or crafted .plus game file that hangs Gargoyle at full CPU until the user kills it.

Linkwarden is a self-hosted, open-source collaborative bookmark manager to collect, organize and archive webpages. Prior to 2.15.0, .github/workflows/check-branch.yml runs on the privileged pull_request_target event and interpolates the attacker-controlled github.head_ref source branch name unquoted into a run: shell script. An unauthenticated attacker can open a pull request from a fork with shell metacharacters in its branch name, causing arbitrary commands to execute in the base repository's privileged CI job before the branch comparison result matters. The job has access to GITHUB_TOKEN and any exposed secrets, allowing secret exfiltration and, when workflow token permissions allow repository writes, modification of repository content. This issue is fixed in version 2.15.0.

Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker. Prior to 6.7, log_http_access in src/webserver/webserver.c writes attacker-controlled User-Agent content to the access log without output neutralization when debug.api is enabled. If an administrator configures files.log.webserver inside webserver.paths.webroot with a filename matching lua_server_page_pattern, an unauthenticated request can plant Lua markup in that log and a later request can cause CivetWeb to evaluate the log as a Lua server page. The resulting commands run as the pihole operating-system user and can access or modify pihole-owned configuration, credentials, databases, logs, and rendered interface content. When the log is not served through the Lua handler, the same unneutralized writer still permits log forgery and downstream log-parser injection. This issue is fixed in version 6.7.

Mattermost Desktop App versions <=6.3 6.0.3 6.3.2.0 fail to validate the SiteURL value returned in a server's client configuration before constructing a server object from it which allows an operator of a server configured in the Desktop app to render the application persistently unusable across restarts via an unparseable SiteURL that triggers an uncaught exception reaching the process-level critical error handler. HomeBox is a home inventory and organization system. Prior to 0.27.0, a HomeBox password change revokes the user's other session tokens but does not revoke the user's API keys, and API keys have no default API-key expiration. An attacker who has obtained an API key can therefore retain full API-level access after the account owner changes the password and can keep that access indefinitely unless the owner discovers and manually deletes the key by ID. Because the password change terminates other sessions, the surviving API credential can evade the owner's expected containment and detection. This issue is fixed in version 0.27.0.
Missing Authorization vulnerability in Liquid Web / StellarWP GiveWP give allows Retrieve Embedded Sensitive Data.This issue affects GiveWP: from n/a through 4.19.2.

SmarterTools SmarterMail Missing Authorization Information Disclosure Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to disclose sensitive information on affected installations of SmarterTools SmarterMail. Authentication is required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of email attachments. The issue results from the lack of authorization prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to disclose sensitive information in the context of a target user. Was ZDI-CAN-33567.

Philips Hue Bridge HomeKit Observable Discrepancy Information Disclosure Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to disclose sensitive information on affected installations of Philips Hue Bridge. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the HomeKit Authentication service, which listens on TCP port 8080 by default. When processing crafted pairing requests, the service discloses internal information via an observable discrepancy between possible responses. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-28470.

NVIDIA OpenShell for Linux contains a vulnerability in the network policy hot-reload component where a local attacker with low privileges could bypass updated network policy restrictions through existing L7-inspected tunnels that continue to use the previous policy after a reload. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to information disclosure and data tampering.

A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to information disclosure, data tampering, and code execution.

NVIDIA OpenShell for Linux contains a vulnerability in its layer-7 REST proxy where a sandboxed actor could bypass the proxy's policy enforcement by sending a request whose body framing is interpreted differently by the proxy and the upstream server, allowing a second request to be smuggled past policy checks. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to data tampering and information disclosure.

A flaw was found in CRI-O. When the optional Linux LinkLogs feature is enabled, the host pod log directory is bind-mounted into a pod emptyDir and is intended to be read-only, but Linux ignores MS_RDONLY on the initial bind and the CRI mount stays writable. A non-privileged UID 0 container can place a symlink at a future kubelet log path so that privileged conmon later appends attacker-controlled log data to an existing host file. This is an append-only host integrity issue, not universal remote code execution; LinkLogs is not enabled by default.

tiny-secp256k1 is a tiny secp256k1 native/JS wrapper. From 2.1.0 until 2.2.5 for tiny-secp256k1 and from 2.2.2 until 2.2.5 for @bitcoin-js/tiny-secp256k1-asmjs, the three-argument xOnlyPointAddTweakCheck path ignores the backend failure return from xOnlyPointAddTweak when a tweak produces the point at infinity. The shared X_ONLY_PUBLIC_KEY_INPUT buffer then still contains the original point, so a caller-controlled resultToCheck equal to that point can make the stale-buffer comparison return true even though no tweaked key exists. Protocols that rely on this helper to validate caller-controlled internal keys, tweaks, and comparison values can accept an invalid derived key. This issue is fixed in version 2.2.5.

Files uploaded through FileUpload or ImageUpload elements are stored in an unguessable sub-folder that remains the same for the whole form session. If storing an uploaded file failed, for example because of a file name exceeding the file system's length limit, the raw error message was shown to the frontend user disclosing the storage path including the unguessable folder name and the server's temporary upload directory. With this information, attackers could determine the public URL of files they upload through the form.

If a form allows uploading files that browsers can execute, such as HTML documents, this could lead to Cross-Site Scripting on web servers that do not apply the Content-Security-Policy recommended by TYPO3 to the form upload target folder. This vulnerability is known to be actively exploited.

The FileUpload and ImageUpload elements of the Form Framework use the property allowedMimeTypes as an allow list of MIME types accepted for upload. An empty allowedMimeTypes list was treated as "no restriction". Forms containing upload elements without any configured MIME type, for example in manually created form definitions or when all MIME types were deselected in the form editor, accepted any file except those blocked by the file deny pattern, which only covers PHP-related file extensions. This allowed unauthenticated users to upload files with browser-executable content, such as HTML or SVG documents, to the configured upload folder, which by default is located in a public storage. If attackers know the URL of an uploaded file (see TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-029), this could lead to Cross-Site Scripting on web servers that do not apply the Content-Security-Policy recommended by TYPO3 to the form upload target folder.

The file dump controller (eID=dumpFile) delivers files, file references and processed files identified by their uid, protected by a token. The token only covered the uid value, but not the type of the requested resource. A valid token issued for a file could therefore be reused to request a file reference or a processed file with the same uid. As a result, unauthenticated visitors could download files, for example from non-public storages, for which no token had been issued.

CodeIgniter4 before 4.7.5 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in the View Parser (system/View/Parser.php) that allows attackers to bypass auto-escaping through re-scanned substitutions. Attackers controlling one rendered value can inject Parser syntax like {other|raw} or {!other!} to emit unescaped attacker-controlled values, executing scripts in viewers' browsers.

Pastefy 7.2.1 before 7.2.7 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in MermaidViewer.vue that passes attacker-supplied %%{init}%% directives to mermaid.mermaidAPI.updateSiteConfig(). Unauthenticated attackers can create Mermaid or Markdown pastes setting securityLevel to loose with a permissive dompurifyConfig to steal viewers' API session keys and act on their accounts.

linkdotnet Blog through 17.1 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect users by passing unvalidated redirectUri values on the Login and Logout pages. Attackers can craft login links sending victims to attacker-controlled sites after authentication, and inject persistent returnTo destinations into other users' logout redirects via the shared AuthInformation instance.

Poppler pdftohtml through 26.11.0 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in HtmlLink::getLinkStart() in utils/HtmlLinks.cc that writes PDF link annotation URIs into href attributes without escaping in HTML output modes. Attackers can craft a PDF whose /URI entry contains a double quote followed by HTML markup or event handlers to execute script in browsers viewing the generated HTML.

OmniFaces is a utility library for Faces. From 5.2 until 5.4.3, applications using <o:sse> or @Push(type=SSE) with session scope, view scope, or a user attribute can expose pushed messages because org.omnifaces.cdi.push.SseEndpoint#doGet accepts a channel identifier registered by SseChannelManager and PushSessionManager without verifying that the caller's HTTP session owns it. An attacker who obtains the victim's channel identifier from a logged URL, report, Referer header, or shared link can connect from a foreign or absent session and receive messages intended for the victim. Application-scoped channels are intentionally unbound, and this issue permits message receipt but not message injection. This issue is fixed in version 5.4.3.

Converting crafted CP949 input to UTF-8 character encoding and ignoring invalid characters, in the GNU C Library version 2.1 or later may result in the converter reading past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling application to crash.

When the CP949 decoder encounters an invalid input byte sequence like '\xa2\xe8' it ends up advancing the pointer tracking the read buffer position twice.  If //IGNORE is set on the destination encoding and this sequence is at the end of the input buffer, the decoder may then end up reading past the bounds of the input buffer.  To exploit this, the target iconv function needs to set //IGNORE on the destination of the conversion and the input and encoding needs to be attacker controlled.

Converting crafted ISO-2022-CN-EXT input to UTF-8 character encoding, in the GNU C Library version 2.2 through 2.44 may result in the converter reading past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling application to crash.

When the ISO-2022-CN-EXT decoder encounters an invalid input byte sequence like '\x0e' it ends up advancing the pointer tracking the read buffer position twice.  If this sequence is at the end of the input buffer, the decoder may then end up reading past the bounds of the input buffer.  To exploit this, the input and encoding needs to be attacker controlled.

Converting crafted input from UCS-4 to IBM1390 or IBM1399 character encoding, in the GNU C Library version 2.3.3 and later may result in the converter reading past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling application to crash.

When converting from UCS-4, these encoders may encounter a combining base such as U+00E6 and jump ahead by 4 bytes to check the next UCS-4 code point.  The check for end of buffer however does not account for this, which may result in a buffer overread if the following code point has less than 4 bytes remaining.  Exploitation of this bug not only requires attacker control of input and encoding, but also strict control over layout of the input in memory.

October System provides the system module for October Content Management System. Prior to 3.7.18 and 4.3.2, the Media Library MediaManager::onCropImage and cropImage path accepts a user-controlled destination filename without applying the default_extensions allowlist enforced by the normal upload path. An authenticated backend user with media.library.create permission can upload arbitrary bytes under an allowed extension and use the zero-dimension crop branch, which performs a byte-for-byte File::copy, to write those bytes into the public media folder under an attacker-selected extension. Default server configurations block PHP execution in that folder, but HTML or SVG output can produce stored cross-site scripting in the application origin; non-default servers that execute PHP in the media directory can expose remote code execution. This vulnerability is fixed in 3.7.18 and 4.3.2.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in ThimPress LearnPress learnpress allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects LearnPress: from n/a through 4.4.13.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Brainstorm Force Spectra ultimate-addons-for-gutenberg allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Spectra: from n/a through 2.20.5.

phpMyFAQ 4.0.12 through 4.0.19, 4.1.x before 4.1.12, and 4.2.0 pre-releases before 4.2.0-RC.1 contain a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in startpage.twig, where top-ten FAQ titles are rendered with Twig's raw filter. Authenticated users with FAQ edit permission can save a question containing a double quote and event handler, which runs script for every start page visitor.

Scalar scalar-ninja 0.1.0 before 0.3.3 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in get_scalar_api_reference() that embeds unescaped OpenAPI content inside an inline script element. Attackers can supply an OpenAPI document containing a </script><script> sequence in content or sources to execute scripts in the documentation origin for every user viewing the API reference.

Scalar scalar-ninja 0.1.0 before 0.3.3 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject scripts by supplying unescaped ScalarConfig title values. Attackers controlling title metadata can close the title element with </title> and inject a script tag that executes in the documentation origin for API reference visitors.

AppFlowy-Web before 0.20.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the TextareaAutosize component that allows workspace members with edit access to inject markup by copying unescaped values into a hidden mirror via innerHTML. Attackers can store a database row title or checklist task containing an element with an event handler to execute script in browsers of users opening the row, including unauthenticated published page visitors.

LaraCollab through 0.18.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated client-role users to inject script by posting unsanitized task comments rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Attackers can post malicious comments that execute when users, including administrators, open the task or view dashboard recent comments, allowing actions in their session.

AudioBookRequest 1.9.0 through 2.0.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to inject script through manual book request fields due to disabled Jinja2 autoescaping. Attackers can submit malicious title, author, narrator or info values via POST /api/requests/manual to execute script in an administrator's browser and access admin-only endpoints.

FS PBX through 2.2.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in FaxesController, PaymentGatewayController and VirtualReceptionistController API routes that only check authentication. Any authenticated user can delete other tenants' fax records by UUID, deactivate or modify the platform-wide payment gateway, and change another tenant's IVR greeting.

Habitat through 1.7.1 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in CreatePostController::addAttachmentsToPost() that allows authenticated users to claim other users' unposted image uploads. Email-verified attackers can submit sequential attachmentIds when creating a post to attach another user's pending image, exposing it publicly and removing it from the uploader's post.

BeikeShop through 2.0.0.32 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows registered customers to inject script by submitting an unsanitized RMA comment rendered unescaped in mail templates. Attackers can submit a return request with malicious script saved to mail_logs.content, executing in an administrator's browser session when they view the Mail Logs entry.

wireguard_webadmin before 0.9981 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in scheduler/views.py that allows low-privilege authenticated users to manage peer schedules without Peer Manager level. View Only or Debugging Analyst users can create, modify, and delete schedule profiles and time slots to disable WireGuard peers or keep disabled peers off.

Filament Curator is a media picker plugin for Filament panels. From 3.0.0 until 3.7.9, 4.1.2, and 5.1.2, the Curator media panel accepts image/svg+xml files by default and stores and serves their markup inline without sanitization. An authenticated user with media-upload permission can store an SVG containing scripts, event-handler attributes, or javascript: URIs. When another panel user selects the View action, the SVG opens as a top-level browser document and its active content executes in the Filament application's origin. The script can perform authenticated same-origin actions as the viewing user and read same-origin data and script-accessible tokens. Panel thumbnails are not affected because they render through an image element that does not execute SVG script. This issue is fixed in versions 3.7.9, 4.1.2, and 5.1.2.

code16 Sharp is a Laravel-based framework for building content-management and administrative interfaces. Prior to 9.23.0, an authenticated attacker can submit an arbitrary PHP class name through the embed_key parameter to multiple embed API endpoints. The application passes the selected class to the Laravel service container, which invokes the class's __construct() method and recursively instantiates constructor dependencies, potentially causing unauthorized integrity or availability effects. The attacker cannot supply constructor parameter values or invoke an arbitrary method. This issue is fixed in version 9.23.0.

code16 Sharp is a Laravel-based framework for building content-management and administrative interfaces. Prior to 9.23.0, an authenticated attacker can call the autocomplete API with a request endpoint that contains the configured remote endpoint only as a substring. The endpoint validation uses an unanchored regular expression, so a different internal route can satisfy the check and be invoked server-side through the autocomplete request. The vulnerable path uses SharpFormAutocompleteRemoteField::setRemoteEndpoint(); applications using SharpFormAutocompleteRemoteField::setRemoteCallback() are not affected by this endpoint-selection flaw. This issue is fixed in version 9.23.0.

A Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability reflected in the GET parameters `cod_primaria` and `cod_secundaria` of the Novanet Web endpoints `NNws_ShwNewDup` and `NPcd/NFG_VerNoticia`. User-provided data is reflected within a JavaScript block without proper sanitization or context-appropriate output encoding. An unauthenticated remote attacker could craft a manipulated URL that, when visited by a victim, would execute arbitrary JavaScript code in the victim’s browser, within the context of the affected site. The flaw resides in the platform’s shared code, so it could affect organizations using that vulnerable code.

The fix for TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-009 was incomplete. GeneralUtility::sanitizeLocalUrl performed its checks on the URL-decoded value, but returned the original, URL-encoded value. URLs containing certain percent-encoded characters therefore passed the sanitization checks as local URLs, although they point to an external host. Applications that use the sanitized URL for redirects are vulnerable to open redirect attacks. This enables attackers to redirect users to external content and carry out phishing attacks. In the TYPO3 core, this affects redirects in the backend, which require the victim to be logged in to the backend.

Backend users with access to the dashboard could therefore make the server send HTTP requests to arbitrary hosts, including internal network services and cloud metadata endpoints, which are not reachable from the outside.

Improper Output Neutralization for Logs vulnerability in the XmlLayout and XmlLayoutSchemaLog4J of Apache log4net.

Both layouts split a message holding the CDATA end marker into several CDATA sections, but searched for the marker with a culture-sensitive comparison. Ignorable characters or a combining mark around the marker made the search miss it, so the CDATA section stayed open. From 3.3.1 on, an XML parser then reads the following log events as part of that message; earlier versions leave the log file not well-formed. A party whose data reaches a log message could hide later log events from a consumer that parses the XML log.

This issue affects Apache log4net: from 1.2.9 before 3.6.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.6.0, which fixes the issue.

advisories.title:
Improper Output Neutralization for Logs vulnerability in the FileAppender, RollingFileAppender, UdpAppender and SmtpAppender of Apache log4net.

Characters the configured encoding could not represent were converted by that encoding's best-fit fallback, which turns fullwidth characters such as U+FF1C, U+FF1E and U+FF02 into <, > and ". The conversion happened after XmlLayout or XmlLayoutSchemaLog4J had escaped the text, so a party whose data reaches a log message could forge complete log events in an XML log, for example a fake audit entry. On .NET Framework this needs no configuration where the ANSI code page is single-byte, since that is the default encoding; on .NET it needs a configured single-byte encoding such as ISO-8859-1. This is the best-fit conversion described by the WorstFit research.

This issue affects Apache log4net: from 1.2.9 before 3.6.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.6.0, which fixes the issue.

advisories.title:
Improper Neutralization of Null Byte or NUL Character vulnerability in the AdoNetAppender of Apache log4net.

Text parameters were bound unchanged, so a NUL character or an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate reached the database as it was. A database that refuses such a value, such as PostgreSQL, rejected the insert and the event was lost; only the first such loss per appender was reported. A party whose data reaches a log message could suppress that event.

This issue affects Apache log4net: from 1.2.9 before 3.6.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.6.0, which fixes the issue.

A time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in the local port selection in AWS efs-utils (amazon-efs-utils) before 3.3.5 might allow a user that can start EFS mounts on a shared host to read and write a different Amazon EFS or S3 Files file system that is mounted on that same host, under that mount's IAM identity and access point, via concurrent mount operations. Only file systems mounted on the same host at the same time can be affected. Every mount involved was configured by the owner of that host, using credentials and access points that owner controls, against file systems whose owners had already granted that host access, so the issue grants no access beyond what the host was already permitted and does not cross AWS account boundaries unless the host's owner configured a cross-account mount. The practical risk is lateral access between workloads on the same host at the same time, for example one container reading another container's file system under that container's identity. The issue does not expose the other mount's IAM credentials or TLS session keys.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade amazon-efs-utils to version 3.3.5 or later. Users of the Amazon EFS CSI Driver should upgrade to version 3.5.4 or later, and users of the Amazon EKS EFS CSI add-on should update to v3.5.4-eksbuild.1 or later.

react-native-webview 13.7.0 through 17.1.0 on Windows contains an unrestricted URI scheme launch vulnerability in the WebView2 OnCoreWebView2NewWindowRequested handler, which passes requested URIs to LaunchUriAsync without scheme or user-initiation checks. Malicious web content can call window.open() or use target=_blank links with schemes like ms-settings: to launch Windows protocol handlers without the external-protocol confirmation prompt.

Attackers with the Employee role can call get_events with empty filters for any date range to retrieve every employee's approved leave applications and shift assignments, including leave types, dates, shift locations and times.

Issue summary: A server configured with the Suite B certificate flag through
SSL_CTX_set_cert_flags() and with TLS 1.3 enabled may read past the end of a
fixed group list when it processes a ClientHello whose supported_groups and
key_share contain no Suite B group.

Impact summary: A remote client can send a ClientHello that makes the server
read past the end of a static array. The values read are never returned to the
client, so no memory is disclosed; on builds with sanitizers or hardened
allocators the read may crash the process, causing Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read

Description: When the Suite B certificate flag is set, OpenSSL restricts the
accepted groups to P-256 and P-384 by substituting a fixed two-element list
for the configured group list. The tuple machinery used for key-share
selection was not updated for this substitution: tls1_get_group_tuples() still
returns the configured tuples, which by default describe eight groups. The
server-side walk in tls_parse_ctos_key_share() then advances through the
two-element list using those tuple counts without checking the cumulative
offset against the number of groups present.

Only applications that call SSL_CTX_set_cert_flags() with
SSL_CERT_FLAG_SUITEB_128_LOS and leave TLS 1.3 enabled are affected. The
openssl s_server -suiteB_128 option sets an X.509 verification parameter
instead, so the stock command line server is not vulnerable. Default
configurations do not reach this code.

A client that offers only groups outside the Suite B set, such as X25519,
forces every tuple to be walked and the read to run past the array. The bytes
read are compared against client group IDs and never sent back, so no memory
is disclosed. On builds with address sanitizers or hardened allocators the
read can abort the process; in ordinary release builds it reads a few bytes of
adjacent constant data.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

When changing the settings of a scheduled export, no permission checks are done to see whether the user making the change has access to the exporter after the change. This way, an attacker with access to change organizer settings and e.g. access to all orders could change the export to refer to gift cards instead, even if they do not have access to gift cards.




The fix for this is technically a breaking API change, since changing the export type of existing scheduled exports is no longer allowed, but we don't expect this to affect any typical API usage.

Incorrect authorization in the credential loading logic in AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes (aws-privateca-issuer) before 1.12.0 might allow an authenticated remote user with permission to create namespace-scoped issuers to obtain certificates, including subordinate CA certificates, signed by another namespace's AWS Private CA with that namespace's stored AWS credentials, via a namespace-scoped issuer that references a credentials Secret in that namespace.



To remediate this issue, users should first copy any credentials Secret they intend a namespace-scoped issuer to use into that issuer's namespace and update the issuer's secretRef.namespace to match. Then, upgrade aws-privateca-issuer to version 1.12.0 or the AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes EKS add-on to version v1.12.0-eksbuild.1.

Incorrect authorization in the credential handling for namespace-scoped issuers in AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes (aws-privateca-issuer) before 1.12.0 might allow an authenticated remote user with permission to create namespace-scoped issuers to obtain certificates, including subordinate CA certificates, from every AWS Private CA and certificate template reachable by the controller's own AWS identity or by any IAM role that identity can assume. This happens because a namespace-scoped issuer that supplies no credentials, or sets only a role, falls back to the controller's own identity.



To remediate this issue, users should first update any namespace-scoped issuers that rely on the controller's identity to use their own credentials. Then, upgrade aws-privateca-issuer to version 1.12.0 or the AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes EKS add-on to version v1.12.0-eksbuild.1.

fzf is a command-line fuzzy finder. Prior to 0.74.5, trigger-driven zsh completion in shell/completion.zsh uses _fzf_feed_fifo to create a FIFO at the predictable shared path ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fzf-complete-fifo-$$ and continues after removal or creation errors. On a multi-user host, a local attacker can pre-create that path as a symlink so the victim's completion stream overwrites a victim-writable file, potentially enabling code execution when that file is later sourced. A pre-created FIFO can instead disclose a bounded stream of completion candidates or block completion. On default modern hosts, fs.protected_symlinks blocks the overwrite variant, and protected_fifos and protected_regular further limit the FIFO disclosure and blocking variants, so exploitation depends on the relevant kernel protections being disabled and on the victim invoking the affected completion. This issue is fixed in version 0.74.5.

The CeliachiaRL integration component distributed with Farmasimplex uses shared OAuth credentials across multiple customer installations. An attacker who obtains the credentials from one installation could reuse them against services associated with other installations, potentially leading to unauthorized access to sensitive information or modification of integration data.

HomeBox is a home inventory and organization system. Prior to 0.27.0, the unauthenticated GET /swagger/doc.json endpoint copies the client-supplied X-Forwarded-Host header into the OpenAPI host field without requiring a trusted proxy or validating the value. An attacker can therefore make the served OpenAPI document direct Swagger UI Try it out requests to an attacker-controlled host. When a shared cache or CDN stores and serves that poisoned document to an authenticated user, Swagger UI sends the user's API requests and bearer token to the attacker, enabling disclosure and modification of the user's HomeBox data. Without a shared cache, the attacker can affect only the attacker's own response. This issue is fixed in version 0.27.0.

Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker. From 6.0 until 6.7, validation in src/api/list.c permits spaces for GRAVITY_GROUPS and consequently skips carriage-return and line-feed validation for group names submitted through POST /api/groups. The unsanitized name is copied into the Location value in pi_hole_extra_headers, and CivetWeb interprets embedded CR/LF sequences as separate HTTP response headers. An authenticated administrator can therefore inject headers such as Set-Cookie, Location, or Cache-Control; when a browser processes the response, this can cause session fixation, attacker-controlled redirects, or cache behavior changes. This issue is fixed in version 6.7.

The SOCKS5 client in subsys/net/lib/socks/socks.c built the CONNECT request in socks5_tcp_connect() by choosing the SOCKS5 address type from the address family of the proxy (proxy->sa_family) while reading the bytes out of the destination address supplied to connect(). A SOCKS5 request encodes the destination independently of the transport used to reach the proxy, so the two families are unrelated and nothing in the path forces them to agree: set_context_proxy() only requires the proxy family to match the socket, and zsock_connect_ctx() enters the SOCKS branch before any destination validation. With an IPv6 proxy and an AF_INET destination the code treated an 8-byte struct net_sockaddr_in as a struct net_sockaddr_in6 and copied the 16-byte sin6_addr from it, reading 12 bytes past the end of the object and transmitting them to the proxy.

With CONFIG_USERSPACE enabled, z_vrfy_zsock_connect() copies only addrlen user bytes into a stack-resident struct net_sockaddr_storage and enforces no per-family minimum length, so the oversized read stays within the storage but returns stale, uninitialised kernel-stack bytes. An unprivileged user-mode thread can therefore open an AF_INET6 stream socket, point setsockopt(SO_SOCKS5) at a proxy it controls, and call connect() with a short AF_INET destination to have the kernel send it 12 bytes of supervisor stack residue per attempt. Without CONFIG_USERSPACE the read runs past the end of the caller's own struct net_sockaddr_in, disclosing adjacent memory to the proxy; the family mismatch can arise unintentionally when a destination is obtained from DNS while an IPv6 proxy is configured.

Impact is limited to information disclosure of at most 12 bytes per connect() call, with no write primitive; the leak is delivered to whoever operates the SOCKS5 proxy. The mirrored pairing (IPv6 destination through an IPv4 proxy) is memory-safe but encoded the destination as SOCKS5_ATYP_IPV4 from the first four bytes of the IPv6 address, causing the proxy to connect to an unrelated host. Exploitation requires the non-default CONFIG_SOCKS option, a socket with SO_SOCKS5 configured, and both IPv4 and IPv6 support in the image.

The fix moves the encoding into a helper that selects the address type from dest->sa_family and validates dest_len against the matching struct net_sockaddr_in/struct net_sockaddr_in6 before copying, rejecting under-length or unsupported destinations with an error.

The REV.exe module distributed with Farmasimplex contains embedded OAuth client credentials for integration with the IZS platform. An attacker with access to the executable could extract and reuse the credentials, potentially leading to unauthorized access to integration resources or manipulation of associated information, depending on the privileges granted and authentication controls in place.

The Envira Gallery  WordPress plugin before 1.16.4 does not apply its own gallery-permission policy until an administrator first opens its permissions screen, instead copying gallery-management capabilities onto each role from that role's core post capabilities after activation, which lets Contributor accounts create, edit and delete galleries that the policy is meant to restrict to higher roles.

The Royal Addons for Elementor  WordPress plugin before 1.7.1071 does not restrict or validate the post meta keys used when counting or rendering a filtered grid, and does not reject private (hidden) meta keys, allowing unauthenticated users to disclose the value of arbitrary private post meta one value at a time from the filtered result count. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-17585, whose 1.7.1067 patch covered only a separate search-based path and left the grid filtering path affected.

The Search & Replace WordPress plugin before 3.2.4 does not correctly restrict which database tables an administrator of a single site may operate on in a multisite network, allowing subsite administrators to read and modify the tables of other sites and of the network, and to make themselves Super Admin.

The Search & Replace WordPress plugin before 3.2.4 does not restrict one of its database tools to network administrators on multisite installations, allowing administrators of a single subsite to run arbitrary SQL against the whole network's database and make themselves Super Admin.

The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not perform a capability or nonce check on an AJAX action available to authenticated users, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to disclose the name and content of non-public templates stored on the site.

The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not verify that the acting user is authorised to modify the target post when saving a template, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor to overwrite the content and type of an arbitrary post, including another user's published page, removing it from the front end.

The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not sanitise post meta saved through an AJAX action, nor escape it when rendering the product page, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor (who lack the unfiltered_html capability) to store JavaScript that executes in the browser of anyone who views the product, including administrators.

The Dynific Addons for Elementor (formerly Anywhere Elementor) WordPress plugin before 1.3.1 does not perform a capability check on an AJAX action that stores a configuration value, allowing any authenticated user, including Subscribers, to store a value that is later output without proper escaping in a quoted attribute on an administrator settings page, resulting in Stored Cross-Site Scripting that executes in the administrator's session.

The WPvivid — Backup, Migration & Staging WordPress plugin before 0.9.140 does not limit its table prefix rewrite to table names when restoring a database backup, which corrupts the length of stored serialized values and allows users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant a PHP object that WordPress instantiates after an administrator restores a backup.

The WPvivid — Backup, Migration & Staging WordPress plugin before 0.9.140 does not prevent serialized data it cannot safely unserialize from being re-serialized as a PHP object during a site migration, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant a PHP object that WordPress instantiates after an administrator restores a backup onto a different URL.

The Contact Form 7 WordPress plugin before 6.2.5 does not check that the post a form submission says it was sent from is publicly viewable before resolving post-related mail-tags, allowing unauthenticated users to obtain the title, URL, author name and author email of private, draft and trashed posts where such tags are used in an email or message returned to the submitter.

The ICRTouch white-label TouchTakeaway Cordova applications do not implement certificate or public-key pinning for backend HTTPS connections. The applications therefore rely exclusively on the device’s system trust store when validating server certificates.
An attacker who can cause a device to trust an attacker-controlled certificate authority, or who operates through a compromised or improperly issued trusted certificate, may be able to intercept and modify application traffic.

The Otter Blocks  WordPress plugin before 3.2.10 does not use URL-aware escaping when it resolves its dynamic data tags inside HTML attributes, which could allow unauthenticated users to post comments containing links that execute arbitrary JavaScript when clicked, for example by a logged-in administrator.

The ProfilePress  WordPress plugin before 4.18.1 does not atomically consume the source subscription when processing a membership plan change, allowing a customer to submit concurrent plan-change checkouts against a single paid subscription and obtain several active memberships for the price of one.

The Hide My WP Ghost  WordPress plugin before 7.0.19 only enforces two-factor authentication on the interactive login flow and not on other authentication paths, allowing an attacker who already has a user's valid password to authenticate as that user without completing the second factor.

The Hide My WP Ghost  WordPress plugin before 7.0.19 does not remove or restrict a debug branch in its output rewriting, allowing unauthenticated attackers to reveal the hidden login page, the hidden admin path and the renamed content folders the Hide My WP Ghost  WordPress plugin before 7.0.19 is meant to conceal.

The RSVP and Event Management WordPress plugin before 2.7.19 does not sanitise and escape attendee data imported from a spreadsheet before outputting it on the frontend RSVP form, which could allow users with the Author role and above to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against anyone, including administrators, viewing the affected attendee, even when the unfiltered_html capability is disallowed.

The Flamix: Bitrix24 and WooCommerce Products Sync WordPress plugin before 1.7.0 does not restrict or validate an unauthenticated file-exchange request, allowing anyone to write a file with an attacker-chosen name, extension and path to a web-served location and thereby execute arbitrary PHP.

The Probono Form Basic WordPress plugin before 1.3.3 does not validate the real type of files uploaded through its public form, trusting the client-declared MIME type instead, which could allow unauthenticated attackers to upload PHP files to a public directory and execute them before they are deleted, on servers that do not honour the Probono Form Basic WordPress plugin before 1.3.3's Apache-only access restriction.

The OneLogin SAML SSO WordPress plugin before 3.7.1 does not validate a user-supplied parameter before using it to redirect an already-authenticated user, allowing unauthenticated attackers to redirect a logged-in user to an arbitrary external domain via a crafted link (e.g. for phishing).

IO::Socket::SSL::PublicSuffix versions through 2.099 for Perl let an on-path attacker choose the installed public suffix list because update_self_from_url fetches it over cleartext HTTP with no integrity check.

Called with no argument, as the module's documentation shows, the updater fetches the list from the `http://` address in the URL constant and checks only that the request succeeded, with no signature or digest over the response. The lines that come back are written into the module's own source file as the built-in list.

An attacker on the network path when the updater runs chooses the suffix boundary the module reports to every caller on the host, and that answer persists in the installed module until it is reinstalled. Dropping one rule makes the hostname check in IO::Socket::SSL accept a wildcard certificate that spans the whole public suffix that rule named.

IO::Socket::SSL::PublicSuffix versions through 2.099 for Perl allow code injection via a fetched list line that closes the built-in data heredoc when update_self_from_url rewrites the module's source.

The rewrite copies the module's source down to the built-in list's heredoc and appends each fetched line below it. Nothing checks that a line looks like a domain. A line that is not a comment loses only what follows a `//` and its trailing whitespace, so a line reading END_BUILTIN_DATA is appended as it stands and ends the data block in the rewritten file. Every fetched line after it is Perl.

Arbitrary Perl runs in every process that loads IO::Socket::SSL, which loads this module unconditionally, until the file is reinstalled. The attacker must control the fetched list, through the cleartext default URL or a caller-supplied one, and the updater must run with write access to the installed module.
